location: p. 3, section 1.3.1 Analysis plan and section 1.3.3 Academic persistence
quote: 1.3.3. Academic persistence ... These analyses showed a significant effect of C1, F(2,191) = 4.62, p ... = .033, β = 0.15, 95% CI [0.01, 0.29]
reason: Canonical primary source verified (Hernandez, Silverman, & Destin, 2021, JESP 92, 104080, DOI 10.1016/j.jesp.2020.104080). The neutral target description explicitly specifies Study 1 academic persistence, for which Section 1.3.3 reports β = 0.15 (F(2,191) = 4.62, p = .033, 95% CI [0.01, 0.29]) on the focal contrast C1 (BSS condition coded +1 vs. active and passive controls coded -0.5), whereas shipped 0.32 (and the prior adjudication) came from a different outcome measure in Section 1.3.2 (endorsement of background-specific strengths, F(2,196) = 22.33, p < .001, β = 0.32). In the covariate-free two-orthogonal-contrast OLS regression (Section 1.3.1), the reported test statistics and 95% CIs satisfy the standardized regression identity β_std = sqrt(F1 / (df_error + F1 + F2)) = sqrt(4.62 / (191 + 4.62 + 0.47)) = 0.1535 ≈ 0.15 with SE = sqrt((1 - R^2) / df_error) = 0.0714 and 95% CI [0.01, 0.29] (whereas the unstandardized contrast slope on C1 with SD(Y) = 0.97 and SD(C1) = 0.68 would be b ≈ 0.22), confirming standardized beta.
